en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Eighth Chapter
Is it the case that the five sense-bases are sensual pleasures?
Yes, they are.
Is it not the case that there is desire associated with that? Yes.
If there is indeed desire associated with that, then surely you should not say: [that there is no such thing].
“The five bases are sensual pleasures.

Is it not the case that there is lust connected with them, desire connected with them, longing-and-lust connected with them, intention connected with them, passion connected with them, and intention-and-passion connected with them? Connected with those...
Is rapture connected with that [feeling], and is joy connected with that [feeling], such that it is "rapture and joy connected with that"?
Yes. If there is indeed rapture and joy connected with that, then surely you should not say: [that it is not so].
“‘The five sense-bases are sensual pleasures’—
is it not to be said that ‘the five sense-bases are sensual pleasures’?”
“Yes, [it is so].
“Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
‘Bhikkhus, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure’?”
Which five?
Forms cognizable by the eye... [and so on] ...
tangible objects cognizable by the body that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire, and provocative of lust.
“Monks, these indeed are the five strands of sensual pleasure.
Is this a sutta? Yes.
"In that case, the five sense-bases are sensual pleasures.
"Are the five sense-bases sensual pleasures?
"Yes."
Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
"Bhikkhus, there are these five cords of sensual pleasure.
Which five?"
Forms cognizable by the eye...
[and so on] ...tangibles cognizable by the body that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire,
and provocative of lust— these, monks, are the five cords of sensual pleasure.
"Moreover, monks, these are not sensual pleasures, nor are these the strands of sensual pleasure; these are called 'sensual pleasures' in the discipline of the Noble One.
"For a person, sensual pleasure is passion for intention;
those variegated things in the world are not sensual pleasures."
"Intentional lust is the desire of a person;
the various [objects] remain just as they are in the world.
Yet, herein, the wise subdue their longing."
Is it indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, it should not be said—
“The five bases are sensual pleasures.
The discussion on sensual pleasures is finished.
